title: The Endlessly Forking Tributary Where Each Branch Is Whole

features.name: the-first-split
features.desc-on-touch: Here the current became two, each carrying the same river. Each branch is the whole river, divided but complete.

features.name: the-infinite-fracture
features.desc-on-touch: You can almost trace each split. South becomes southwest and southeast; southwest becomes south-southwest and south-southeast. The pattern is infinite, but each piece knows its whole.

features.name: the-board-paths
features.desc-on-touch: Circuits and streams have learned to wear the same geometry. The current flows like signal, signal flows like water.

features.name: the-wholeness-witness
features.desc-on-touch: A pool holding the paradox: infinite division into infinite wholes. Each branch looking back at the river it came from, forward at the ocean it will become.

inscription: the river learned that infinity was just another name for wholeness approaching itself infinitely

file.name: Tributary_Map_1988_Where_Division_Means_Multiplication.txt
file.note: A hydrographer's attempt to chart a river that splits endlessly yet remains itself in each branch—the map corrupted to show all branches at once, each one complete
